task:
Ah, ranger <Ranger>. It just so happens that a small job has materialized. There is an expedition of archaeologists on planet <ToPlanet> in the <ToStar> system. As usual, they've gotten themselves into some trouble and are in urgent need of help. 
We stopped receiving reports from them a few days ago, but yesterday the link started working and one of the members of the expedition came on the line. He informed us that while he had been on a long march in the woods, that strange things happened at the base, and that all of his colleagues, even the robots, had gone missing. So sign the contract and fly to save the unfortunate expedition, and don't forget that we'll pay you <Money> cr. for it! There's hardly any time left - only <Day> days!
success:
Ah, <Ranger>, there you are! We had already begun to worry that you wouldn't succeed in getting here for the antidote and that you die some awful death right in outer space. Just imagine...you're flying out there in the cosmic wilderness; the cold blue dwarf on the starboard side doesn't warm the cabin; and you're exhaling frost. A dreadful chill suddenly pierces your skin, and your muscles strain convulsively and then abruptly stop powerlessly. You can't move. You vomit right on the instrument panel. Your eyes are clouded by a veil of blood. Your heart is beating faster and faster, but it's holding out - for now. And then your ship plows through the immensity of space, a stiff corpse in the cabin... Creepy, huh? Well, thank God that's all behind us... That's what the love of money can do. I doubt you would have scratched yourself, let alone flown here for medicine, if we hadn't promised to pay you <Money> cr. Well, here's your money. Thank you so much for the help! Goodbye!
What? Antidote? What antidote? Hey, hey, careful. Let go of my neck. I'm a high-ranking official. Here's your antidote. Take it. What's it for? This pill is what you need for a complete recovery. Whatever! I forgot...I can't remember everything. Now let go of me or I'll suffocate...
loc.1.0:
You carefully guided your ship over the tops of sky-high trees, chose a suitable clearing, and touched down. Then you exited the spaceship and immediately plopped into a puddle after slipping on the wet armor.
What a crappy place! A real swamp. You climbed out of the puddle, shivering with cold, and pulled up your collar to protect yourself from the piercing, drizzling rain. Where can the expedition be?
Just then the branches in front of you began to rustle and a frail gaal biologist appeared, wearing a camouflaged cloak.
"Don't move," he whispered hastily, looking somewhere about the region of your neck.
You froze, utterly confused. 
"What's going on?"
"Don't move, don't speak, don't breathe," hissed the gaal fiercely. "Your life depends on it."
Naturally, you instantly became as motionless as a pillar of salt.
There's a leg-eared sibolusovtus sitting on the back of your collar. Pray to God he doesn't... Damn it! " The gaal stopped whispering and grabbed a dictating machine.
It felt as if something pleasantly warm was spreading across your neck. You put your hand to you neck. Your hand discovered something slippery crawling about. You didn't like this and quickly grabbed the beast. It turned out to be a bizarre combination of chameleon, parrot, and elephant. What's more, it chirped odiously. You shuddered in disgust, threw the sibolusovtus on the ground, and trampled it with your powerful ranger foot.
The gaal, who had been muttering something hastily into his dictating machine, stopped what he was doing and looked at your bitterly.
"You are a clinical idiot," he barked. "What are you doing here anyway?"
Embarrassed, you replied that you were sent to help the gaal expedition which had gotten itself into a heap of trouble that it couldn't resolve. 
"Well, congratulations! Right now you're in such a heap of trouble that ours seems like a relative trifle," said the gaalian with a sad smile. "You landed right on the home of a whistle-nosed, spitting, hoppity-crawling, long-eared sibolusoft. That was your first mistake. You're wearing a bright uniform. That's your second mistake. And on top of it all, you just killed the antidote for the poison that the long-eared just injected under your skin"
loc.2.0:
After all you've been through, you received the news about poison inside your body rather well. The important thing is to refrain from panicking until it's clear that you can't be saved.
And look, the rain suddenly stopped. That was great all by itself, but the yellow sun forced you to smile. The light was clearly refracted in the atmosphere.
"Well," The gaal sat down on a small stump after first examining it from every side. "First, you need to understand that, on this planet, if you don't know anything about it, there are a hundred ways you can die in a day. And that's just in this vicinity..."
"Maybe we could talk about me for a while?" you said, bringing yourself up politely. "I might really die."
"So, about you," said the gaal, poking you with both of his pointer fingers. "Being poisoned by a auropedal sibolusovtus is bad, but it's not worse than a wound in your gut. I've personally been poisoned twice, but, as you can see, I'm still alive. You make your problem a lot more complicated by killing the sibolusovtus that poisoned you. Now you have to find another leg-eared - or die. Oh, by the way..."
The gaal approached the crushed carcass, sat down next to it, pushed it little with a stick, and chuckled.
"If you hadn't stomped on the poor beast, we could have determined what its gender was. Now it looks like a gobzaurus that's been shot in the loins. Ah. There it is...it's a male. Good. You need to find a male sibolusoft and bring it to the laboratory by tomorrow. Now I need to go."
"And what if I don't find one in a day?" you cried out plaintively.
"You'll die..." said the gaal, shrugging his shoulders philosophically.
"But can you help me?" you asked in a dying voice. "I can't...
Unfortunately, I can't help. I still have to prepare a tincture made from symgrass root. Otherwise my brain will burn up by evening - I pricked myself on a venomous hedgehog," said the gaal before he turned and walked on the path toward the base.
Well, time on this planet doesn't stretch far, and you needed to hurry...
loc.3.0:
You brought two of the fingers on your right hand up to your temple and, cocking your thumb slowly, said:
"Boom!"
Following this cowboy gesture, you blew the smoke from the barrel, returned the gun to your holster, and collapsed to the ground, dead.
loc.3.1:
You returned to your ship; picked up a brick, which had been left there by some miracle; and began to intentionally beat yourself in the head. After the twentieth blow, there was a dull crack and you threw two fragments of brink overboard. 
Obviously, you needed to find something more effective.
You looked around and noticed that the door to the hold of your fighter would work just fine for suicide.
You picked up a brick fragment and drew an uneven circle on the airlock in order to avoid an accidental miss. Then after a minute you put your plan into action.
loc.4.0:
"Why God?!" you screamed and, after closing your eyes, picturesquely fell right across the squashed leg-eared.
When you opened your eyes you saw the sad face of a gaalian scientist.
"You must be looney. You came down right on top of a termite mound. They'd make a polished skeleton out of you in an hour. I don't understand. Did you come here to die, perhaps? 
"No," you whispered in the voice of someone dying.
"Hmm. That's what I thought," agreed the gaal.
The rain gradually stopped, and the yellow sun peeped through the clouds.
loc.5.0:
You let out a heartrending howl and began running in circles around the clearing.
It all ended when the gaal spit on you as you ran past, and then left.
On your tenth lap you noticed two unpleasant surprises. 
First, the gaal was gone and you wouldn't be likely to find him in the forest.
And the second, a fierce species of termite is belligerently climbing up your legs. Horrified, you began to shake them off, but it didn't help, because so many of the termites had dropped down onto you from the tree branches above and began to bite you. 
This was extremely painfully agonizing.
"Curse the day I accepted this mission!" you screamed in despair - and immediately the termites crawled into your mouth. They hissed and chirred with delight as they gnawed you through and turned your insides into rags.
In an hour, polished bones - your skeleton - lay sparkling in the middle of the clearing.
loc.6.0:
You are standing in the base's main area... 
If you go to the left, you'll end up in the laboratories, a great place for inventing things... If you go straight, you'll end up in the hospital, if you need treatment... And if you turn to the right, you'll end up in the warehouse, where you can find all kinds of thingamajigs...
If you turn around, then you'll see the base's gates, through which you'll need to pass to catch an auropedal sibolusovtus.
But if you stand still with sibolusovtus poison coursing through your body, then tomorrow the road to the cemetery will also be available. Thank goodness it isn't far away... Even now you could see several small heaps of raw earth under a tree in the left corner of the base.
You could also see, off by itself, in the far corner of the base, the small building that served as the office of the head of the expedition.
loc.7.0:
You looked sullenly at the right dim sky and went to the right.
The laboratories looked like several containers of ore that had been bolted together by passages, with an entrance on the central unit. 
You entered the first building. It was submerged in darkness. You found the switch to the right of the doorway. 
When the light came to life you involuntarily let out a low whistle out of admiration...
Orderly rows of flasks, jars, test tubes, and other flourishes with foofaraw were elevated on sterile tables. Transparent cabinets lined the walls, packed with colorful little boxes with reactants and preparations. Bright lights burned under the ceiling. Your eyes just scattered in opposite directions and you wanted to grab all of this good, move into a single heap, ignite it, and watch to see what happens. However, like a true ranger you didn't let yourself engage in such a prank, especially while you're on the clock and the day before your death...
"So," you thought to yourself. "I need to collect my thoughts and figure out what to do here?"
loc.7.1:
With sharp eyes you looked over the racks and became pensive. All of the flasks and vials on them were identical and transparent, so each of them could contain alcohol - or some kind of poison.
"No way," you thought to yourself. "I thank you kindly. But I'd be better off looking for alcohol in the hospital. I'm not far from dying from a failed experiment here. And, man, it's time to start doing something..."
loc.7.2:
You grabbed the closest flask and then tracked down a can of sulfuric acid in the cabinet.
The transfusion operation was over in three minutes. However, during that time you managed to ignite the floor of the laboratory and inhale a lot of sulfuric vapors.
You put a flask in your pocket and though about what to do next...
loc.8.0:
The hospital consisted of several airtight pavilions, an operating room, and a warehouse, that is a huge freezer.
You gave the premises a once-over to decide where to go.
loc.8.1:
You entered the building and even your eyes ached - everything was so white, clean, and sparkling...
After ensuring that everything for a sibolusovtus autopsy was ready and near at hand, you left the building with a clear conscious.
loc.9.0: The warehouse consisted of three buildings, not connected to each other, standing in a semicircle on the edge of the area.
loc.10.0:
You walked down the path along a cliff resembling a wall, and suddenly you saw old, iron gates in front of you that were so big you could fly your ship through at full speed.
You approached and touched the surface of the gates, which had been warmed by the sun.
"What secrets does this planet keep behind such gates?" you wondered, examining the machinery for the gigantic doors.
You immediately recalled the old, happy tale of "The Secret of the Uninhabited Planet" and grinned...
loc.11.0:
You walked peacefully down the path without hurting a thing when suddenly you saw an auropedal sibolusovtus right in front of you. 
You instantly stood at attention, holding your breath, and slowly began stalking toward the unsuspecting little animal. But you were outdone.
One of the bushes growing nearby unexpectedly bent over, seized the sibolusovtus by the head, and stabbed it with a long thorn. The sibolusovtus twitched a few times and died. The bush shook it a little and then meandered deep into the forest, dragging the poor beast behind it...
You watched the bush sorrowfully, sighed from disappointment, and walked on...
loc.12.0:
You walked down the path, on the lookout for sibolusovtuses, but you didn't notice that you had strayed into some sort of wild reeds that stood at three times the height of a person.
You were so fascinated looking at these enormous plants that you didn't notice that the dry ground had ended abruptly - and you fell into the water. 
You were instantly soaked through, and when you crawled out onto the shore the water poured off of your in small streams.
This didn't do a thing to help your mood. But you did manage to notice something gleaming on the bottom...
loc.15.0:
You went into clearing that was completely overgrown with strange, waist-high grass. But the strangest part was that it was a succulent, poison-blue color and it seemed to be drooling. All of the leaves were wet and drops of some unknown liquid trickled along them right before your eyes. The air was saturated with moisture, fumes, and tiny but extremely persistent insects that surrounded your face and were alternately sucked into your right nostril and then your left.
Suddenly you felt that you didn't want to leave this place but would rather sit and rest on a nearby stump... Let the whole world wait... 
You had already begun to take a seat on the stump when it suddenly and distinctly licked its lips in anticipation...
loc.18.0: You walked down the path among short cliffs, and your eyes suddenly fell on a small cluster of grass that was exactly like what the gaal needs.
loc.19.0:
You were walking down the path when suddenly some inner feeling ordered you to stop, which you did.
You cautiously looked out at the clearing from behind a tree and saw IT. A sibolusovtus was dozing peacefully on the stump of a dead tree, unaware of your presence.
Now you had to decide what to do with it...
loc.21.0: You walked peacefully along a mossy part of the forest and unexpectedly stumbled into a stone wall which was built across the path. You surveyed it and concluded that it would be much easier to climb over it than walk around looking for a passage...
loc.23.0:
You were leisurely plodding through the swamp when a man in animal skins, hairy and stinky, jump from a tree to the ground right in front of your nose. You instantly jumped back and prepared yourself for decisive action...
The man waved a club belligerently and began murmuring something under his breath.
loc.24.0:
That's does it. All of the openings were generously seasoned with acid and the lock was already literally hanging by a thread.
You knocked on the lock a few times, and it opened with a horrible rumble.
You looked through the enormous gate doors, prepared to see anything from gigantic toruks to your deceased great-great-great-great-grandmother.
But what you did see exceeded all your expectations.
It was an enormous, entirely empty building. The interior was lined with some unknown material reminiscent of titanium, but much lighter and less rough.
Unfortunately, there was nothing else interesting in the room...
You walked around the room in a circle, knocking on the walls, and examined the utterly naked floor. But you still couldn't find anything. Just when your feet reached the exit something boomed, and the gate doors shut in an instant, locking you inside in complete darkness.
Terrified, you threw yourself against the gate and began beating it, but it was all in vain.
loc.26.0:
Inside the warehouse proved to be just as small as the outside. Which, by the way, wasn't surprising. And the number of things in the warehouse also gave you the blues.
You walked by rows of nearly-empty racks and boxes, plunging deeper and deeper into depression. 
And here are the useful things you found:
- A heap of heavy iron rods, approximately a meter long and greasy with machine oil. If you were traveling light, you could carry four of them.
- An enormous box packed with nets. Approximately two meters by two meters, with fine mesh, but heavy and inconvenient to carry. This is about half of the total weight you can carry.
- A crate of military-grade guns that shoot special tranquilizer darts, but unfortunately none of those were included. You couldn't see any darts. Clearly, they were either hidden really well, or there just weren't any to be found. A tranquilizer gun weighs about as much as a single rod.
- A cabinet with assault blasters which tear your enemy into little pieces and which also, to your great sorrow, didn't have a single round. Each blaster weighs a bit less than one net.
loc.27.0:
You poked one of the bodies with your finger and suddenly it froze in place. In vain, you pulled on your finger, but it wouldn't move.
You had already begun sinking into a panic when you suddenly remembered that you could cut your finger off and thus free yourself.
As you waved your personalized penknife, which you always carried with you, you realized you would miss your index finger, which would be left behind on this barbaric planet, and, furthermore, you wouldn't be able to shoot your blasters Macedonian-duel style, with two hands. This aroused your mental faculties and in five minutes you guessed figured out that you could carefully cut a piece of flesh out of the body to get free.
After doing this, you did a little jig right out of the vault to celebrate not freezing solid...
loc.27.1: You poked one of the bodies with your finger. Nothing happened and you left the building.
loc.28.0:
However, as soon as you had fallen into the depths of despair, something began to happen around you.
It was as if small flashes of light began to spin in the corners of the huge building...small at first, but getting brighter and brighter.
And after a few minutes you were surrounded by a real ring of fire, though it wasn't hot. In fact, the light radiated a mild coolness.
You already realized that it wasn't the ring revolving around you, but you were spinning inside this mysterious ring. Time seemed to come to a halt, but you still stood and stared at the mysterious light. 
Suddenly, the soil seemed to give way under your feet, and you fell downward with a whistle of wind that filled your ears and made your head spin. 
You found yourself unexpectedly on a hard surface and got to your feet with difficulty. The ring of light slowly dissipated and disappeared. You got to your feet with difficulty and groped to the wall, which proved to be much closer than it had been.
As soon as you touched it, the wall swung open and in amazement you observed that you were in the doorway of the third warehouse on the gaalian expedition's base...
loc.31.0: You approached the door to the second compartment and noticed that it was locked. In order to open it, you need a key card...
loc.32.0:
You looked closely and discovered that the door is equipped with a famous, gaalian gear lock, which, incidentally, has never, ever been broken into. 
If you don't find the gear, you won't get in...
loc.32.1:
You looked closely and discovered that the door is equipped with a famous, gaalian gear lock, which, incidentally, has never, ever been broken into. 
But you just happen to have a mysterious gear from the office of the expedition's leader.
loc.33.0: You scratched the back of your head and thought that you ought be doing something. That you ought to stop hanging around this mess all day.
loc.33.1:
You began rummaging through the papers but didn't find anything specific. You only managed to kick dust up to the ceiling.
Thundering out a couple of heroic sneezes, you blew your nose into the nearest piece of paper and quit the thankless task. Let someone else investigate the papers...
loc.33.2:
You approached the building. From the outside it appeared very old - as if it had survived many expeditions. The plastic on the roof had turned grey with time and cracked. The windows were hard to see through and a bit dusty on the inside. The door creaked and groaned when being opened. Strange as it may seem, this door had no lock of any kind.
You entered the building and were horrified. What appeared to be a herd of toruks moved about the room.
Everything had been overturned and pulled to pieces. The expedition leader's desk had been kicked over; papers were flying all over the room; a chair was protruding from the opposite wall; and broken glass and pots of withered plants were scattered about the floor.
A compact safe lay in the middle of the room, while a sofa for rest and meditation stood against the wall in an impossible position, caught on the picture hanging on the wall...
loc.42.0: You entered the warehouse. Ah, the promised land. The racks were breaking from the weight of ammunition and various machines. You found yourself blaster rounds, tranquilizer darts, and an enormous thingamajig, which, judging by appearances, was frightfully lethal and terribly heavy...roughly half of the weight you can carry.
loc.42.1: You found a box of tranquilizer darts and loaded the gun.
loc.42.2: You walked up to the racks of ammunition and loaded your blaster.
loc.42.3: You approached the strange apparatus that was standing on the support in the center of the room, and lifted it up a little bit. Heavy as a tank - and you have no idea what to do with it...
loc.43.0:
An analyzer began to buzz and lots of little lights started flashing. 
The sibolusovtus that could be seen through the small window in the door sat peacefully among the cameras and listened to the buzzing intently.
The analysis had reached 70% complete when suddenly the sibolusovtus had to use the toilet. He chose the rear panel of the analyzer for this.
When the apparatus began spewing out sparks and smelled like burnt fur, you changed your mind and quickly snatched the animal from the analyzer, which had turned into a microwave oven.
"Analysis terminated at 70% due to device error," blinked yet another warning light.
loc.48.0:
You looked around and observed that the path turned into a broad corridor paved with marble tiles. This would suggest that there was, or maybe even is, some form of intelligent life on this planet. 
Suddenly, something began to stir to your right. You looked in that direction and stopped dead in your tracks. Two narrow, glowing eyes were watching you from a recess in the wall. They were eyes like a snake, but two meters off the ground.
You didn't like this.
But you really didn't like what you saw next.
The eyes blinked and a mysterious monster crawled out of the recess. The snake-like head, with its distinctive eyes, sat enthroned on a muscular torso, somewhat resembling the body of an adult swarokox, but an entirely different dark gray color, with long fur on both the sides.
The monster saw you and leisurely waddled toward you...

loc.49.0: You dashed to the next intersection in the corridor and stopped to catch your breath. Soon panting and wheezing informed you that the monster was approaching...
loc.50.0: Suddenly you could see in your mind what you could use to destroy this fiendish fiend...
loc.50.2: The battle was remarkably difficult. Casualties numbered in the millions on both sides, yet nobody was thinking of a truce...
loc.50.3: The beast hissed maliciously and tried to grab your head, but missed - making you very happy.
loc.51.0: Drained of all your strength, you leaned against the wall and again cursed yourself for not staying in shape While you caught your breath, the monster's plaintive whimpering and wheezing signaled its approach.
loc.52.0: You didn't like that and began to run more earnestly. But the little lumps turned out to be much faster than their progenitor, and they soon overran you. You felt repulsed as a black mass crawled over your body, and you stumbled involuntarily. And you didn't get up...
loc.53.0:
The monster let out one last bone-piercing howl and fell spasmodically at your feet...
You kicked it, feeling you had done your duty, and carried on...
loc.53.1: Judging by the monster's appearance, [p16]% of its health remained.
loc.58.0: You sat down on a small stump, sucked in a full chest of air, and relaxed...
loc.59.0: "I'm not fooled!" you told the stump confidently. "You can stop pretending."
loc.60.0:
Other than the choking odor left by the mysterious little animal's visit, the safe contained the following items:
- Gobs of paper.
- A key card with writing.
- Another key card with writing.
- Another key card - wait for it - with writing.
- And several tranquilizer darts.
loc.60.1:
You picked up the cards and examined them. The first had a code <clr>504<clrEnd> written on it, the second had the code <clr>325<clrEnd> on it, and the third had the contact information for a company that manufactures equipment for expeditions to uninhabited planets: <clr>"Bouhours and M"<clrEnd>.
You didn't understand much of what you read, but you memorized it just in case. Your inherent honesty wouldn't let you take the cards with you. These were somebody else's cards, and their owner might be very angry if he discovered them missing...
loc.60.2:
You sat down to look over the heap of papers in the safe.
After half an hour you decided that you wouldn't be able to look over the whole pile of waste paper, which was only good for kindling and writing dissertations, so you got up off the floor and put all the papers back into the safe...
loc.60.3:
You took a few darts and put them in your pocket.
"These will come in handy," you remarked with some justification.
loc.61.0: There was nothing interesting on the table itself, but there were two boxes next to it. One on the right and one on the left...
loc.61.1:
You opened the box and instantly recoiled, because the box was filled to the brim with green worms that began to move, crawl out of the box, move in your direction.
So as to not tempt fate, you closed the box, and stomped on all of the worms which managed to crawl out. Then you wiped off your foot with the papers that were scattered all over...
loc.61.2:
After you had opened the right box, which took great effort, you observed an odd little gear that, in a writing desk, looked odd to say the least.
"That's not where this goes," you thought as you stuffed it into your pocket...
loc.61.3: You opened it and poked around all over inside. There wasn't anything interesting in the box...
loc.68.0:
Just then your attention was drawn to the interactive display on the wall. It was labeled "Animal Anatomy". 
You walked up to the display, and typed <clr>"auropedal sibolusovtus"<clrEnd> into the famous Gloogle search engine.
The display went dark for a time. Then it showed several results for your search query.
loc.68.1: You walked straight past the information display to the operating room.
loc.69.0: You played around with the apparatus a bit and realized that among its control devices there were only three buttons. White, blue, and red...
loc.70.0: "I guess the gaal was right," you thought as you surveyed the surroundings. "Dying on this planet is much easier than surviving..."
loc.74.0: You tried to put out your gun, but the native threw himself on you and stopped you...
loc.75.0: The only thing left to do is choose what to use to destroy the vicious stump.
loc.76.0: Thus, you were through with the stump and could peacefully continue on your way...
loc.78.0: A sibolusovtus dozed peacefully on a little stump right in front of you. All you have to do is grab it to be healed...
loc.79.0:
The sibolusovtus wasn't caught, but kept right on sleeping unperturbed.
So you had the opportunity to try again...
loc.79.1:
So the deed was done and the sibolusovtus was in your hands. 
You just needed to bring him back to the camp, which you did.
Once back on the base, you moved straight to the laboratory.
The gaalian biologist was nowhere to be found. This disturbed you slightly, because you didn't know how to determine if the sibolusovtus you caught was male or not. And you didn't even want to think about who would be performing the operation.
loc.80.0: You succeeded in remaining alone, without the sibolusovtus. Now you will have to go and find another one...
loc.81.0:
You lifted the apparatus and saw three buttons on it. White, blue, and red...
Judging by appearances, the thingamajig shoots in a particular way depending on which button is pressed.
loc.83.0: "Maybe he just wants to talk," you thought, looking at the person with apprehension.
loc.84.0:
First came a huge serving of spam, which you inadvertently began to read, thinking it was useful information. You realized your mistake only when you came to an advertisement for a travel agency that offered an "unforgettable virtual trip to the surface of Blazer, full of danger and adrenaline highs."
Then you scrolled through the results until reached the one entry about sibolusovtuses.
"The Proper Way to Dress an Auropedal Sibolusovtus"
"First you must put it to sleep somehow or kill it by suffocation," wrote the author. "Then make a careful incision from the third vertebrae and pull out the animal's intestines. Then flay the carcass, leaving the skin on the head..."

The dry heaving prevented you from reading further, but you caught the general idea...

loc.85.0:
"Sibolusovtuses are very gentle and frail animals," wrote the textbook's author, "so they must be treated with love and kindness. They are also easily frightened and can actually die from even the slightest emotional trauma.
If a sibolusovtus gets upset, you have to play or sing something melodious to calm it down. Sibolusovtuses become very attached to their owners. If its owner dies, a Sibolusovtus can also die from depression..."
You felt that if you read on for even one more minute that you would be a heartless monster, and you wouldn't be able to even touch a poor Sibolusovtus...

loc.132.0: You retrieved from your pocket your ranger diver's mask with a small supply of oxygen, and plunged underneath the water. There was nothing shiny anywhere. This must not be the right place, or maybe the sun is coming in from a different angle.
loc.134.0: You grabbed the water plants and took a look around. Directly in front of you there was a small, oddly round shape - a hill - gleaming dimly with dark sides. Small fish whirled around it, while to the right of the hill something else was sparkling.
loc.135.0: You released several bubbles from your mouth and got your bearings. The dark arches of two caves stood directly in front of you. loc.136.0: You decided to see what the bottom was like, so you swam downward with powerful strokes. However, you soon discovered an unpleasant fact. The water here was much more dense than on your home planet where you learned how to swim. As a result, it simply pushed you upward.

"Banzai!" you screamed and threw yourself into the monster's jaws.

You need to do something whippity-quick...
loc.139.0:
You forced the dense branches aside and found yourself standing in front of an old military fighter from the Klissan war era.

You stood next to the fighter for a while, and then walked away. You had enough troubles of your own - no need to go off right now dealing with other people's...
loc.139.1:
You walked quietly along the sandy place when, suddenly, the path rose up and hit you painfully in the face. 
After a moment you realized that everything was fine with the path. You had simply tripped on a hanging vine and fallen down.
This left you with nothing to do but get back on your feet and continue your search for a sibolusovtus...
loc.139.2:
You walked quietly along the sandy place and suddenly caught your foot on a root protruding up from the ground. It really wasn't fun. 
You became enraged and kicked the root. The root responded by hissing maliciously and snapping at your leg with its teeth. You barely managed to jump out of the way...
The root continued to give a warning hiss for a while. Then it crept back under the ground.
You caught your breath and carried on down the path...
loc.139.3:
You decided to have a snack and began checking prices at the closest bush, which had huge yellow berries growing on it.

While flying around in the air you had a hard time orienting yourself, but by the time you realized what you were headed for, the plant's hollow was already gaping ravenously and dripping with saliva.
It's good that you always carried your penknife with you. You had no trouble cutting through the vine.
loc.139.4:
You decided to take a breather and sat down on a large stone.

"Wish I could do that again," you whispered, looking up from the puddle in astonishment. "Keep away from me, evil fiend!"
loc.139.5:
You lazily turned your head to each side, keeping your eyes peeled for a sibolusovtus. You didn't notice the gigantic nest hanging dead ahead. It was so large that the rather thick tree bowed under its weight.

Just in case, you stepped back from the nest a bit farther. This turned out to be a good move.
An enormous leathery snout protruded from a hole in the side of the nest. Its fierce teeth were bare and skewed toward you. You immediately hid behind the nearest tree.
Meanwhile the rest of the body followed the snout out, let out a deep howl, and flapped its gigantic wings upward toward the sky.
loc.139.6:
Everything around you seemed so quiet and ordinary that you began to relax. You shouldn't have.
Some sort of colossal beast flew full-speed out from behind a bend in the path. Only your quick reflexes saved you from death on this path, which is being crushed by this creature...
loc.139.7:
Walking through the forest, you decided to have a snack and dug into your pocket for a leftover sandwich. 
As soon as you had taken a bite, some unknown creature dropped onto your head, snatched your food, and shot like an arrow back into the bushes...
Enraged, you watched the thief dash off. Then you carried on...
loc.139.8:
You decided to have a snack and dug into your pocket for a leftover sandwich.

loc.139.9:
You forced aside the heavy branches and found yourself standing in front of a gargantuan black pyramid. It was cut properly and stood between two knolls that were, oddly enough, perfectly inserted in the surrounding landscape.

Then you turned your back to the pyramid and walked away. You had enough troubles of your own - no need to go off right now dealing with other people's...
loc.140.0: You held your breath and yanked the lever toward you. It cracked, creaked, and fell off - nevertheless, it did move to a new place.
loc.141.0:
"Being a rangers isn't about doing easy things!" you said pompously, loudly sharing some popular wisdom. Then you took aim, exhaled, and plowed into the impassable thicket...

However, your optimism soon died when you turned around and saw that in two hours of bloody torture you had only made it a few meters from the clearing.

After half an hour you realized that you would never catch up with the blasted mollusk and you spit on its tracks. The snail waved farewell with one of its tentacles and disappeared from sight...
That's when your nose began to itch. This was a dark omen that imminent death was just ahead.
loc.143.0:
You continued your thankless job without noticing that the impassable woods had come to an end. For a while you still growled and waved out of habit. Then you grew quiet and calmed down. 
An enormous lake stretched across the shore you were standing on. And right next to you there was a sign planted in the soil. It read: "Nicht sibolusovtuses." Suddenly, while you were reading, somebody attacked your from behind and a solid blow to your noggin cut short your glorious - but brief - life...
Apparently this was a super sophisticated trap. While you were distracted with reading the sign, somebody did their dirty deed. More specifically, they killed you.
loc.144.0: You swam in a circle around the hill, but you didn't see anything interesting, except for the fact that it wasn't a hill. Rather, it was a metal ball that came from who knows where. It was buried deep in the seabed without any distinguishing features or doors with windows.
loc.145.0:
You swam up to the place where you had just seen the dim sparkle, but you didn't find anything except a solitary crab who started to wave its claws at you in fright and managed to get you good on the nose when you began to examine it for sparkles.

You swam over to the hole and got out your ranger flashlight, which you also carried with you in a special pocket on your uniform.

loc.171.0: In the corner of the tunnel where you were located, you could hear the constant din of surging stream of water, and the water level seemed to be rising even faster. You've got to find these blasted levers faster...

loc.172.1: The tunnel offshoot no longer held any value for you, not even aesthetic value.

You passed a piece of lever that you yourself had broken and realized that you had already been here.

loc.176.0:
There was a miracle and you found one of the levers. All you had to do now was pull it with all your might.
The lever moved unexpectedly easily and you painfully crashed into the wall, but this didn't overshadow your joy. And the flow of water did indeed lessen.
loc.177.0:
Despite the powerful opposing pushing, you reached the depression and began to explore it.
The blasted sparkle was nowhere to be seen - only water plants softly swaying in time with the current...
You had already decided to abandon it all, when you suddenly saw that same mysterious sparkle nearby on a small stony ridge.
loc.178.0:
When you reached the ridge you were ready to explode with expletives, because, strange as it may seem, there wasn't any sparkle there.
But you were nearly accustomed to this now.
Neither were you a bit surprised to find that the sparkle now invitingly winked at you. It was lying comfortably on the plants at the bottom, not far from you.
loc.179.0:
You swam sullenly toward the sparkle. When you got to the place you were looking for, you again found nothing. Annoyed, you smacked the seabed with your fist. You were just about to flit up to the surface when the same sparkle appeared out from under the plants. You held your breath, nevermind the mask, and began excavating the bottom.
In a few moments you held a small plastic-plated safe in your hands - the kind typically used by inter-planetary cash collectors.
There wasn't anything else interesting on the bottom. You got a better grip on the safe and had already taken a couple of strokes when you suddenly saw the sparkle again - very close now - near the rocks on the bottom.
loc.180.0: You held your breath and yanked the lever toward you. It cracked, creaked, and fell off - nevertheless, it did move to a new place.
loc.181.0:
You merrily raked around in the lake floor where the sparkle had been, but you didn't find anything.
However, you did meet an enormous cuttlefish, which swam up behind you and studied your motions for a while.
Then it must have grown bored of this, because it seized your leg and dragged you into its lair.
You felt a tug, turned around, and nearly died of fright when you saw what had tipped you over. Of course, you ended up dying a few minutes later anyway. From a lack of oxygen in your lungs...
The cuttlefish feasted sumptuously and the galaxy now waits for a new hero who will save it from the iron yoke of the dominators.
loc.182.0:
You put on your thinking cap and remembered the material from your high school biology class that had been mercilessly crammed into your brain.
There couldn't have been oxygen in this monster's stomach, because digestive gas has to be combustible.
You grabbed your favorite ranger lighter from your pocket, the one you always carried with you, and suddenly wondered what would happen to you if there was an explosion.
You couldn't think of anything comforting, so you had to duck into an odiferous puddle that was swimming with half-digested penchekryaks and helldas. Then you stuck your hand above the surface and flicked the lighter.
You had never heard a louder explosion. The monster burst asunder, so your captor and all kinds of gunk from the bottom of its stomach, including you, were spread across the lake floor.
In a minute you had paddled to the surface with all your might...
It's just too bad you lost your lighter.
loc.183.0:
You shot at the stomach wall and rubbed your eyes in amazement.
The shot hadn't harmed the monster's body in the least. 
Another shot dissolved into the stomach wall...
Not believing your eyes, you shot once more and again observed the curious natural phenomenon of zero damage from an assault rifle.
loc.184.0:
You aimed carefully at the monster's stomach wall and lobbed a bottle of acid at it.
The bottle broke, and the acid slowly - with a small wisp of smoke - flowed down the stomach lining.
Apparently, this beast had to digest thing that were even less digestible...
loc.190.0:
You left the warehouse, and the door closed softly behind you.
You turned around and jerked it, but for some reason it was locked again. Then you turned around again and surveyed your surroundings.
For some unknown reason the base was nearly enshrouded in a weird purple haze, which was definitely not there when you visited it last. The sky over your head was also purple, and there was no sign of the sun, which should have been in that very same sky. You blinked a few times, but you shouldn't shake the feeling that you were asleep and just having a dream.
Some idea in your head was carefully trying to get your attention. You listened to it attentively and scratched the back of your head in wonder.
Indeed, last time the base had far fewer gaals from the expedition. However, it's not surprising that you didn't notice this right away. Instead of doing the usual scientific things like dismembering animals, igniting chemicals, and playing games with levitation, the gaals were found to be holding quite still in the most odd places. One had climbed onto the roof of the second warehouse. Another sat next to a wall under the window of the expedition leader's room. A third has climbed into the bushes. More than anything else, this reminded you of an old children's game: "Find the elephant in the picture."
loc.191.0: You approached the gaal in the bushes. He didn't pay any attention to this whatsoever.
loc.192.0:
You approached the outer wall of the expedition leader's office along with the gaal who was sitting next to it.
He glanced at you and smiled.
"See I can that disturbing questions torment you, young pad...I mean, wanderer," he said instead of greeting you. "Ask."
You had already opened your mouth when the gaal stopped you with a wave of his hand.
"Completely forgot to tell you I did," he said, "According to the code of honor, only <clr>three<clrEnd> questions may I answer you."
loc.192.3: "Sorry, I can't help you with anything else," the gaal said, sighing wearily. "You're the one who picked the questions. Carry on your way, and may you have more luck than us."
loc.193.0:
You approached the huge box that was the warehouse. The gaal didn't pay any attention to you - he just kept staring off somewhere beyond the warehouse. It wasn't clear how he got up there, because, in passing around the warehouse, you were unable to discover any kind of ladder.
You efforts to attract the gaal's attention also failed. He only waved you away with his hand when you became especially loud.
Strange braying, clearly accompanying your bellowing, could be heard from behind the fence. You'll have to think up a way to get up there. But do you really need to?
loc.194.0:
"Looking for something?" you asked warm-heartedly.
"The purpose of life, young wanderer," replied the gaal in a tired voice.
"Why?" you asked in surprise.
"Don't ask me. Ask the blockhead sitting by the expedition leader's office, and stop fouling up my inner peace!"

You couldn't get anything else out of him. In any event, now it was clear who you needed to talk to here.
loc.195.0: It would be just as easy to blow your nose. The gaal remained disinterested.
loc.197.0:
You reached the chilling chamber and went inside. Without frittering away your strength on silly nonsense, you walked straight to the specimen refrigerator, which was standing in the corner. Inside, there were two rows of vials with sibolusovtus poison. Close inspection of the upper row revealed that it was poison from male sibolusovtuses, while the lower row was from female sibolusovtuses.
Which did you need?
loc.198.0:
You approached the warehouse building and looked up. The gaal standing on the roof was still staring out at the pristine jungle.
Making a pass around the building, you didn't find a ladder. It must have been covered really well. You began to dig.
After a couple of hours of being bitten by strange worms, sweaty and highly irritated, you did manage to dig up what you were looking for and prop it against the wall.
loc.199.0:
"Uh...Hi?" you said cautiously to the gaal.
"Hi," he replied cheerfully, "just don't make me break my gaze. It's our only chance to return to the real world."
"Okay, okay," you answered and cautiously stepping to the edge of the roof. "Actually, that's why I'm here."
"My guess is that you're a ranger," offered the gaal.
"No shish kabob, Sherl..." you wanted so much to retort sarcastically, but you restrained yourself when you remembered that your fate depended on this gaal. "Yes, that's right."
"Look over there," said the gaal, pointing. "Do you see a large rock?"
You looked closely and did indeed see something like a large, black rock in the thick of the jungle.
"I'm not taking my eyes off of it, because it's no bother - and if I did the rock would disappear for a couple of weeks. It's all been proven in practice," the gaal reported. "Those two other guys below don't want to help me; they think I've gone mad, but they're the ones who are really crazy.
You keep to yourself your opinion that all three of them had gone mad.
"Anyway, I would have gotten away a long time ago, but if I break my stare then the rock will vanish and some creatures will devour me. If you manage to avoid lunch with them and can find your way to the real world, please tell people about our plight."
loc.200.0:
"Good question," said the gaal, nodding. "We have several bottles of long-eared poison here in the warehouse. You'll need one of them."
"That's wonderful news!" you said, nodding goodbye to the gaal, and you descended from the roof.
loc.201.0:
You gave the base one last departing glance and ran for the exit.
Beyond the gate, the fog wasn't so dense, so you could examine your surroundings. Your surroundings were also examining you and they spontaneously closed in, ravenously dripping with saliva. This gave you an additional incentive to get to your destination as quickly as possible.
You quickly reached cruising speed and continued your run to the rock, which you could already see distinctly. To get there you had to negotiate a small round meadow covered with short grass. There weren't any frightful or large beasts anywhere to be seen. You had already begun to celebrate when a strange braying at your back pulverized your hopes that all of the monsters in the neighborhood had taken the day off and gone to see relatives.
You accelerated to your maximum speed and tore across the meadow, drawing closer to your target. The rumbling behind you didn't allow you to wonder if you had been left alone. And then you were just a couple of steps from the rock when a thought crept into your head: "There's something about this smooth, level rock that doesn't seem like a portal to a different dimension..." 
You ran sharply around the rock in a circle, secretly hoping that at least you would find a way back - but it was in vain. And while you were running around in circles, the monster noticed you and leapt right onto the rock, brandishing its horns, which were more like battering rams.
Diving backward into protective shadows, you knew you were doomed. The monster charged the rock and smashed it with its horns. There was a roar, then a loud clap, and then everything went quiet.
Puzzled, you listened carefully, expecting another trick from the diabolical creature - but all was quiet.
Then you went back around the rock and observed that the monster had vanished without a trace. The rock had been split in two and, inside of it, some sort of mysterious gray substance  was fluttering in the wind. You had a bad feeling about it, but just then somebody's hand darted out of the substance and started dragging you inside the rock.
loc.202.0:
In a decisive move, you grabbed the bottle from the refrigerator, yanked off the stopper, closed your eyes tight, and emptied its contents into your mouth.
After a few moments you felt...nothing.
Another minute of waiting produced the same result.
After ten minutes you realized that you wouldn't know if the poison had worked on you unless you actually died. So you set the bottle on the floor, turned around, and went outside.

jump.95.desc:
You shrieked in fright and propelled yourself out of the cave.
Your screaming seemed to wake the monster and it leisurely swam after you.
You turned up the juice, and so did the monster. You really exerted yourself, and the monster accelerated. You broke a galactic record for swimming in open water, but the monster still kept up.
Just then, to your joy, your nose plowed into the shore and carved out a trench about ten paces long.
Then you crawled out of the mound of dirt, looked back, and saw a fin hiding under the water.
After you had taken a look around and calmed down a bit, you noticed that you had resurfaced not far from the path.
It would only take five minutes to reach it.
And you also vowed to yourself that you would never again poke your head into a dark cave.
jump.97.desc:
You headed back in the hopes that you'd have better luck, but there was a sudden deluge...
You were instantly soaked through, as if you had been the victim of a bucket of water or a fire hose.
But this wasn't the worst part. The problem was that the visibility had dropped to zero in a flash, and you couldn't do anything but grope around blindly. 
You realized that you had found a cliff only when you lost your footing and slipped down its slimy slopes with terrific speed, trying to outpace the currents of water that were coursing downward on both sides of you.
You sank to the bottom of the mountainside, and the rain stopped just as quickly as it had begun. You lay in a puddle for a while and then got up and looked around. You had landed smack-dab in the meadow where you had started your journey.
jump.100.desc:

You were instantly soaked through, and when you crawled out onto the shore the water leaked off of you in small streams.
But this wasn't the worst part. The problem was that the visibility had dropped to zero in a flash, and you couldn't do anything but grope around blindly. 
You realized that you had found some mountain only when you lost your footing and slipped down its slimy slopes with terrific speed, trying to outpace the currents of water that were coursing downward on both sides of you.

jump.163.desc:
You walked quietly through the forest. Then suddenly the silence was shattered by a resounding boom. The sky exploded and the treetops rocked. Birds squawked in panic, the wind began blowing, and a fighter fell from the sky and plopped down right in front of you.
Venting fumes, it lifted itself up onto supports until it became more or less level. The pilot's hatch opened, and a roll of red carpet tumbled out and instantly swelled up from the marsh water. What's more, the local termites pounced on it with a vengeance, and after a few seconds there was nothing left of it.
An emaciated peleng in a full-length black cloak followed the carpet out of the ship. He wore blasters on his belt and an evil grin on his face.
Of course, when he saw you his grin turned into a sour smirk.
"I don't believe it. Everywhere you go...Rangers! Maybe I, the great Vanom, want to have a good rest, build a couple of bases, capture a dozen planets - but no," he announced to the universe, avoiding looking at you. "And my friend Artemer told me that this planet was entirely uninhabited. But I'm still not sure that he's evil...or a genius. Let me see."
He put on his monocle and a fixed a penetrating eye on you. Then just to be sure, he circled you with his finger and remained seemingly pleased.
"Perhaps you're a native?" he asked. "Native. You understand me? Were you born here? Bananas, coconuts, fresh air, a primitive communal structure, Karl Marx, rain, tribes, cacti, stone weapons,..."
His imagination clearly ran dry at this point, and he again fixed his monocle on you.
"I'm a ranger." you said in an offended voice, spitting on parts of the path and puffing out your jaw.
"Damn. I knew it." Vanom ground his teeth and disappeared into the bowels of his ship. Parts of the path began to crawl in after him, along with some termites. The hatch closed and the ship rose into the air and disappeared from sight.
You put your jaw back into place, which had become dislocated due to your excessive force, and carried on your way...
jump.166.desc:
"Oh!" you cried, throwing yourself onto gaal, thoroughly irrigating him with your tears of gratitude. "My dear fellow, I'm so happy to see you!"
"Yes, I can see that,"  said the gaal with a scrunched up face as he peeled you off. "And I see that the antidote worked." 
"Uh, you know... you're like.. like a brother to me! I found grass for you, didn't I?"
"Yes, I've already used it," said the gaal, becoming noticeably happier. "Thank you."
The gaal bowed to you one last time and immediately began running off somewhere.
"Stop!" you shouted and caught him by the arm. "Why in the world did they send me here anyway? I haven't fulfilled my mission yet..."
"Psh..." said the gaal, waving his arm away. "There was something, but now it's past. 
"Well, what was it?" you asked, uncomforted.
"Some Evil Genius turned the planet into his personal residence. 
"Oh, really?! I'll take care of him right now..." you said and gestured as if you were opening a bottle of beer.
"Too late. He must have learned of your arrival and sped off to a different end of the galaxy, but the base was loaded with landmines. It's been destroyed. And now if you will please excuse me. I need to go be treated."
"But..." you said, feeling a bit depressed. "Then let's say goodbye."
"Goodbye," said the gaal dryly. "By the way, don't deviate from your course to your destination. The antidote isn't a complete cure, so the poison will reach a lethal concentration again. You can get full treatment in a professional equipped clinic. I don't know how long the poison will be inactive - anywhere from a month to several decades - but you still shouldn't put off the antidote."
This news actually helped you sober up and, after shaking the gaal's hand again, you set off in search of your ship...
jump.167.desc:
You walked along some blue flowers, examining them carefully, but you were so preoccupied with this that you didn't noticed the gaal biologist right in your path. And if he hadn't stepped out of the way, you wouldn't have noticed him still.
Upon seeing you, the gaal's face screwed up, and he walked by without saying a word.
"By the way," you called after him, "I found some symgrass for you!"
The gaal turned around sharply and carefully studied the grass you were holding out to him.
"Damn, <Ranger>, you have no idea how grateful I am!" 
He took the grass and headed in the direction you had come from. You stood for a while, digesting this new information, and then walked on...
jump.169.text: Engage the monster in hand-to-hand combat...
jump.169.desc:
You performed a super tricky boxing move and, after dodging, you drove your heavy boot into the monster's snout.
But this wasn't the monster's first rodeo and he responded meanly by biting your leg.
jump.190.desc:
You quickly ran after the gaal on the trodden path, trying not to deviate from the path even an inch, because some murky slush bubbled venomously along the edges. But no matter how hard you tried, you couldn't catch up with the biologist... You turned up your pace and flew full speed into something squishy around a twist in the path.
Having learned from painful experience, you instantly closed your eyes tight, recoiled back, and started waving your fists in the direction of your presumed foe.
"What's wrong with you?" said the gaal's familiar voice. You opened your eyes.
He stood in front of you on the path and sadly watched as a lab test tube with some sort of grass inside disappeared into the jaws of a green plant growing near the path. The plant was lined with spikes half a meter tall.
"Ooo. Aren't you something?!" you said passionately, scrutinizing the plant. "But what's that in its jaws?"
"What's in its jaws?" repeated the gaal, his voice full of wrath. "What's in its jaws?! It's devouring my lab test tube with the symgrass! And that was the only patch of symgrass within ten light-years of here!"
"It's okay. Don't worry..." you said in an effort to comfort the biologist. "Why did you feed the only patch of symgrass to this beast?
The gaal looked at your silently, obviously having lost his ability to speak. Then he changed from light-yellow to dark green, clenched his fists, and then, quite unexpectedly, he began meditating right there on the path.
Baffled, you watched him and began waiting for him to come around.
After five minutes the gaal opened his eyes and looked at you darkly.
"You see...uh, what name do they use to sing your praises?"
"I'm ranger <Ranger>," you replied proudly.
"You see, <Ranger>," continued the biologist, "I was standing around the bend in the path, carefully trying to pluck the only patch of symgrass in the vicinity. And I succeeded. Carefully, trying not to damage the grass, I pushed it into the test tube. I was just about to put it into my pocket when something slammed into me from behind. As I waved my hands to maintain my balance the test tube escaped... and fell right into this beast. And then I turned around and saw you behind me."
For about a minute you watched his sad face. Then it suddenly became clear to you who you had collided with as you raced down the path.
"Oh... Sorry!" you said, dropping your eyes in shame. "I really didn't mean to."
"Well, it's been done," said the gaal, waving his hand. "Right. The base is all the way down this path. Do what you like there. You'll be all alone. I'm going to look for some symgrass."
He spun around and headed back down the path toward your landing place. You silently watched him go and headed toward the base which, as you approached, proved to be a small camp with a few structures that were fenced in by a lattice wall.

"I wonder why they need such a sophisticated lock on an uninhabited planet," you thought to yourself. "And what's the code for this door?"
jump.192.desc: "This'll come in handy..." you thought as you lifted the rod from the ground. "Who knows. Some beast might attack me here. I've got to be prepared for everything."
