jump.213.desc:
You shuffled off through the forest, carefully avoiding the holes with bubbling liquid. Suddenly something rocked you to one side and then the other, as if you had been drinking a lot of vtequila. Your head buzzed as if you hadn't eaten in a week, and your legs folded underneath you.
You didn't understand what was happening to you. These must be the effects of the poison the sibolusovtus injected into you. After thinking this, you observed that everything had passed, as if nothing had happened at all. You got to your feet and rotated your head. Everything was in order. Then you stood for a moment, expecting another attack, but everything was still in order, so you carried on...
jump.214.desc:
You passed through two cliffs standing close to each other and suddenly heard strange voices behind the thick trees. The voices were shamefully familiar. You cautiously crept toward the trees and peeked through the dense foliage, pushing it aside with your hands.
In the middle of a dark meadow, there were two shadows: a smaller, emaciated one, and a second much larger and more muscular one.
"And where's he been roaming?" asked the big shadow. You instantly recognized the voice of Organdok, a famous maloq ranger. You wondered what he was doing here.
"I have no clue where he disappears to!" answered the second voice in alarm, which you recognized to be that of the gaalian biologist.
It seemed weird that these two were here together.
Meanwhile, Organdok had grabbed the gaal by the chest and shook him so violently that the poor biologist's head nearly snapped off his skinny neck.
"Listen!" whispered the gaal, "He's still going to be dead by tomorrow morning. He's been poisoned by a sibolusovtus, and I hounded them all down and hid them this morning. He won't find them. An awful death is definitely in his future!"
Unable to contain your anger, you charged into the meadow like bison to figure out what was going on.
You were surprised out of your mind when, instead of two humanoids, you saw two old stumps in the meadow - one big and one small, all tangled with vines and covered in moss.
Amazed and utterly confused, you approached the stumps and prodded the damp wood with your finger. There could only be one explanation. The sibolusovtus poison had upset your nervous system and you were hallucinating. It wasn't fun, but it did give you an extra incentive to work faster to find a leg-eared fiend...
jump.215.desc:
You walked up to the net, glancing at it with a critical eye. Then you removed it from the hooks it was hanging on and wound it up all higgledy-piggledy. Then you looked again at the shapeless mass in your hands even more critically and sighed, clearly at a loss as to how to drag it around with you.
Your only consolation was that it would be very easy to catch a sibolusovtus with a net like that.
jump.217.desc: You took the gun from the rack, looked at it all over, clicked the hammer a few times with a heavy heart, bemoaning the lack of tranquilizer darts, and stuffed it into your belt. It'll come in handy when fighting off monsters. You can beat them with the grip. If you can't find any darts...
jump.222.desc: You closely examined the bulky monstrosity from every side and even felt a twinge of nostalgia for the old, happier days of your youth when every self-respecting ranger had one of these guns.
jump.223.desc:
You entered a small meadow, which swelled to a small hill in the middle.
Moving closer, you took a seat on a small stump not far from the hill in order to shake out the crap that had worked its way into your shoes during your long strolls through the forest.
You were leisurely plodding through the swamp when a man in animal skins, hairy and stinky, jumped from a tree and landed right in front of you. You instantly jumped back and prepared yourself for decisive action...
"Let's go," grumbled a voice behind you and the gunstock jabbed deep into your back.
"Where?" you asked.
"Look to your right," replied the gun-toting stranger. 
You looked to the right and saw that a passage into the hill had appeared. Apparently that's where you were going.
When you entered the passage you realized that you had no clue what was going on. It was an iron tunnel, illuminated by powerful lights, with turrets jutting out from the walls.
"Keep your mouth shut - you'll catch your death!" advised the stranger behind you and jabbed the gun barrel into your back again. You screwed up your face, but you walked on.
The corridor quickly came to an end. Farther on there were numerous rooms, probably laboratories, which were packed with people wearing white medical coats poking around in various intricate machines.
"Don't turn your head - you'll dislocate your neck!" advised the stranger again.
You steadfastly endured the subsequent blow to your ribs, since the object of your travels was now very close.
You approached some luxurious doors at the end of the corridor. For how big they looked, you could fly a fighter through those doors.
Your escort entered a code on the door lock and it popped open.
There was a chair with a tall, carved back facing you at the head of a super-sized table. 
"Who's this?!" resounded a booming voice from every corner of the huge room.
"A trespasser, my lord!" respectfully reported the character who had been leading you. "He was trying to break into the base!"
"Who?!" roared the voice, even more fiercely. "Wonderful! Finally, they're giving the respect we deserve. That's why they sent such a good agent to deal with us!
"What should I do with him, my lord? asked your escort, exuding even more veneration.
"Feed him to my mini-piranhas! We'll let them know who's master of this world!" said the still unseen stranger in the chair, nonchalantly. Then horrible laughter rang out. "MWAA-HA-HA-HA!!!"
Hearing this serenade sent a shiver through your body.
Your guide jabbed you in the back and led you out of the room. You caught hold of the door, but he grabbed you by the scruff of your neck and dragged you farther down the corridor.
When you came to the end of the corridor, he opened the last door and you could see that you were standing above an enormous reservoir that was swimming with the carnivorous mouths of gargantuan fish. 
Wailing, you jerked backward, but your guide was on his guard, and with one powerful blow he sent you tumbling below...
When you regained consciousness you noticed that you were whole and unharmed. And what's  more, you were lying in a large puddle in the middle of a forest meadow with an enormous green worm staring at you with bloodthirsty eyes.
You instantly leapt to your feet and walked away sheepishly. The only explanation for what happened was that the poison in your blood had caused you to hallucinate...
jump.229.desc:
You walked along some blue flowers, examining them carefully, but you were so preoccupied with this that you didn't noticed the gaalian biologist right in your path. And if he hadn't stepped out of the way, you wouldn't have noticed him still.
"Aha," you said and immediately grabbed him by a button. "Would you please tell me how to get into the warehouses? Those tricky little locks you have there are a real pain."
"The first warehouse opened with a code. The code is in the expedition leader's office. The second opens with a key card which I happen to have with me. Here, take it." He offered you a key card. "And the third... Hmm," he began thinking. "Our mechanic installed some intricate apparatus on the third. I've never been inside, so I don't know about it. You'll have to figure it out on your own..."
He detached your hand from his button and walked in the direction you had come from. You stood for a while, digesting this new information, and then walked on...
jump.231.desc: You stepped sorrowfully away from the door, cursing these strange archaeologists who pack things where needed; but where it's not needed, they put tricky locks and other machines that are entirely unnecessary.
jump.232.text: Open the warehouse with the key card...
jump.232.desc: You inserted the key card you had taken from the gaal into the slot on the lock, and the door opened.
jump.233.desc:
You walked up to the storage room's heavy door, pulled with both hands, and opened it, though with some difficulty. A puff of fumes escaped and dispersed instantly in the air. 
You peered in. The carcasses of dissected animals, which the gaals were evidently studying, hung inside. There wasn't anything else interesting in the storage room...
jump.234.desc:
You walked up to the storage room's heavy door, pulled with both hands, and opened it, though with some difficulty. A puff of fumes escaped and dispersed instantly in the air. 
You peered in. The carcasses of dissected animals, which the gaals were experimenting with, hung inside. You carefully moved aside the first row of carcasses in order to see if there were a lot of them there, and suddenly you saw something that made your heart hammer wildly in your chest.
Among the animal carcasses was hung the corpse of a dismembered gaal. You cautiously entered the storage room and examine the poor wretch. 
"So this is what happened to the other members of the expedition! The biologist lost his mind and killed them!" you thought in a fit of enlightenment.
Suddenly it seemed someone was standing behind you. You whipped around, but there was nobody there. When you turned back toward the gaal's corpse, you were amazed to discover that it had vanished and there was a frozen penchekryak hanging in its place. Dumbfounded, you poked it with your finger. The penchekryak was indeed real. Evidently, all the shocks you've endured left you entirely sick in the head...
jump.235.text: Go away from the storage room...
jump.241.text: Collect rounds for the assault blaster...
jump.253.desc: You quickly climbed over the wall and jumped down to the other side.
jump.254.desc:
You walked along the wall, examining it and trying to find an entrance.
When you had begun to feel quite exhausted, you finally found an entrance... 
You pass through it and found yourself on the other side of the wall.
jump.255.desc:
You ran along the corridor to save yourself from the monster, who pranced after you, smacking and drooling and howling in anticipation of lunch. Despite your best efforts, you weren't able to outrun it. 
What's more, maybe it was just your imagination, but the monster seemed distended, as if it had been inflated with air; and you further noticed that this didn't make it run any slower, rather it howled and drooled at the more...
jump.259.desc:
You ran along the corridor to save yourself from the monster, who pranced after you, smacking and drooling and howling in anticipation of lunch. Despite your best efforts, you weren't able to outrun it. 
What's more, maybe it was just your imagination, but the monster seemed distended, as if it had been inflated with air; and you further noticed that this didn't make it run any slower, rather it howled and drooled at the more...
jump.260.desc:
You ran along the corridor to save yourself from the monster, who pranced after you, smacking and drooling and howling in anticipation of lunch. Despite your best efforts, you weren't able to outrun it. 
What's more, maybe it was just your imagination, but the monster seemed distended, as if it had been inflated with air; and you further noticed that this didn't make it run any slower, rather it howled and drooled at the more...
jump.261.desc: The monster, who was still leisurely shuffling after you, stopped abruptly and let out a wild howl. You turned around and saw that it had cut its own chest to shreds. The sight even made you feel ill. Meanwhile, a hole formed in the monster's chest and small slimy lumps crawled out in every direction.
jump.262.text: Whack the monster with the iron rod...
jump.262.desc: You moved a bit closer to the monster. Then you did a fake move and, after dodging its claws, you clubbed it with the rod as hard as you could.
jump.274.desc:
You thought that this must be your imagination. After all, science hasn't proven the existence of stumps with eyes.
The air was so nice and cool that you dozed off...
jump.275.desc: You looked even more closely at the stump. It immediately covered its eyes and hid its fangs, but this didn't disturb you...
jump.278.desc: You walked up to the safe and cautiously opened the door a bit. A sharp, suffocating odor hit your nose and you staggered back. It's a good thing you did. Some kind of crazy beast jumped out of the safe, chattered maliciously, and spit some caustic muck on you. Then it leapt out through a window that had been broken by a chair.
jump.279.desc: You cautiously peered into the safe, fearful that some other beast had taken up residence there... Discovering that this wasn't the case, you sat down in front of the safe and began to examine its contents.
jump.280.desc: You tore yourself away from looking at the chaos going on in the building and left the building.
jump.282.text: Rummage through the papers on the floor...
jump.291.text: Whack the monster with the iron rod...
jump.291.desc: You moved a bit closer to the monster. Then you did a fake move and, after dodging its claws, you clubbed it with the rod as hard as you could. But you didn't take into account the fact the beast had another paw.
jump.294.text: Shoot the monster with the incomprehensible thingamajig...
jump.295.desc: You pushed the blue button as far as it would go and watched in delight as a blizzard slammed into the monster's chest, freezing it and dropping the overall surrounding temperature...
jump.296.desc:
You pressed the white button and watched what it did to the monster.
What it did was most unfortunate. The monster entirely ignored your efforts and gave you a thorough thrashing...
jump.297.desc:
You pointed the weapon's barrel at the monster and pressed the red button as far as it would go.
The air was suddenly filled with the smell of burning fur, and the weapon in your hands issued a toxic blue flame that devoured living flesh...
jump.298.desc: You took aim and fired at the monster that was bounding toward you. Only green slime came splattering out in every direction...
jump.299.desc: You took aim at the monster bounding toward you and pulled the trigger. An opening appeared in the serpentine head of your opponent, but it was still alive and continued barreling toward you...
jump.300.desc: You shot the monster with the tranquilizer gun, but it must have been immune, because not only did it not fall asleep, but it began galloping after you with twice the energy...
jump.302.text: Throw the net over the monster...
jump.302.desc: You threw the net over the monster, and a second later bits of it came sailing toward you. The rest decorated your opponent's paws and head.
jump.304.desc:
You shrank away from the stump and then stepped away for quite a distance. The idyllic atmosphere had disappeared instantly and you lost all desire for sleep.
You spit at the stump's eye from a distance, but missed. Then, utterly unglued, you set off to find a sibolusovtus...
jump.305.desc:
You watched happily as a lovable striped insect crawled along a small leaf on the nearest plant. It was climbing to the very top of the plant, where you noticed a nest belonging to some sort of teensy weensy birdie that has less than half the size of the insect.
"I wonder what will happen," you thought, "when this little brute makes his way to the top of the leaf."
Suddenly, something stung you in the lower part of your back. You sprang to your feet and looked around. But you didn't see anything, so you sat back down...
jump.306.text: Shoot the stump with the assault blaster...
jump.306.desc: You shot the stump, and it joyfully splintered into kindling...
jump.307.desc:
You shrank away from the stump and then stepped away for quite a distance. The idyllic atmosphere had disappeared instantly and you lost all desire for sleep.
You spit at the stump's eye from a distance, but missed. Then, utterly unglued, you set off to find a sibolusovtus...
jump.308.desc:
You continued to sit on the stump and revel in the excellent weather.
Meanwhile, the insect had become distracted from its intentions at the top of the leaf. Now it was smacking and chewing away at the edge of the leaf...
You felt another indistinct prick, but saw nothing when you looked down...
jump.309.desc:
Evidently, the insect had had enough, because it spit out the bit that it until then been gobbling up with relish. Then it again began climbing upward.
The pricking from the stump was now happening almost constantly, but you were too captivated by the scene with the crawling little bugger do look away...
jump.310.desc:
The insect, finally, reached the top of the leaf and curiously probed into the bird's nest with its feelers. The little bird shot out of its home like a bullet and began to flit about the intruder, chirping angrily.
The insect gawked at the bird and blinked a few times, until information about an unidentified stimulus apparently reached its bite-sized brain. Then it abruptly threw open its enormous jaws - which were lined with long, thin fangs like needles - and gulped the bird down. 
This sent a chill down your spine. 
You decided it was time to get to work and got up from the stump... Or rather, you wanted to get up.
You observed that it had anchored to you and wouldn't let go. You threw a fit, but you didn't manage to do anything...
jump.312.text: Shoot the stump with the tranquilizer gun...
jump.312.desc: You planted a tranquilizer dart into the stump, but you couldn't understand what this did for you. Nobody has ever thought to put a tree to sleep...
jump.313.text: Hit the stump with the iron rod...
jump.313.desc:
You swung good and hard and whacked the stump with the rod. 
But since the tree was made out of wood, nothing bad happened to it. Except maybe a small scuff mark...
jump.314.text: Throw the net over the stump...
jump.314.desc: With the accuracy of a sniper, you tossed the net over the stump. It wasn't clear what this gave you other than a ruined net...
jump.315.desc:
You began to suspect that something wasn't right with this strange plant and, stepping away from it, you decided to engage in wholesale slaughter of all of the nearby stumps...
The stump noticed this and, growling savagely, it hurled its roots at you. which came flying up out of the ground. But they weren't even long enough to reach you...
jump.318.text: Throw yourself onto it as quickly as possible...
jump.318.desc:
You issued a war cry and threw yourself onto the poor little beast sleeping on the small stump.
While you were running toward the stump, dreadfully churning your legs, the sibolusovtus had long since woken up and prepared itself to repel the attack of the uninvited guest.
When it spit some kind of sticky gunk into your eyes, you realized that you had underestimated your enemy.
And by the time you had cleaned out your eyes enough to see anything, the sibolusovtus had vanished without a trace...
jump.319.desc: You hunkered down, held your breath, and stealthily tiptoed toward the utterly unsuspecting little beast...
jump.320.text: Throw the net on the sibolusovtus...
jump.320.desc:
The sibolusovtus squealed, shrieked, kicked up its hind legs, stamped its hooves, fidgeted, scampered about, and tried to bolt - but the net pressed it securely to the ground.
You began to gloat, but the brute suddenly pulled it together and began chewing through the net. 
This was part of your plan, so you whacked the sibolusovtus over the head with a heavy rock that was lying nearby.
After this physical effort, the sibolusovtus went limp and let you celebrate in peace.
jump.321.desc:
You took the assault blaster from you shoulder and shot the serenely sleeping sibolusovtus. 
Judging by the gory scrap of a hide left on the stump swimming in blood, you shouldn't have done that...
jump.322.text: Throw sulfuric acid at the monster...
jump.322.desc:
You lobbed a vial of sulfuric acid at the monster. 
This caused the monster to begin fuming and producing awful sounds that caused a sudden quaking in the knees...
jump.323.text: Throw sulfuric acid at the monster...
jump.323.desc:
You lobbed a vial of sulfuric acid at the monster. 
This caused the monster to begin fuming and producing awful sounds that caused a sudden quaking in the knees...
But it didn't stop it from slamming you against the wall several times...
jump.324.text: Throw sulfuric acid at the stump...
jump.324.desc:
You hurled a vial of sulfuric acid at the stump and happily observed that it was just as effective on the stump as it was on the laboratory floor.
"Perhaps they even made the floor out of this wood," you thought to yourself.
jump.325.desc:
You aimed carefully at the little animal and fired.
To your horror, you missed, but the sibolusovtus, who had been roused from slumber by the loud shot, hopped to its feet, chattered angrily, and took off running. 
You tried to catch up, but failed...
jump.326.desc:
You aimed carefully and shot the sibolusovtus with a tranquilizer dart.
The little animal twitched and instantly went limp as it sank into sleep...
You happily picked it up and went to the camp...
jump.327.desc:
You aimed carefully at the sibolusovtus and fired.
To your horror, you missed your mark, but the sibolusovtus just scratched itself in its sleep, giving you a chance to correct your blunder by knocking it out with your next shot...
jump.331.desc:
You pressed the white button on the gun and relished the result.
The sibolusovtus suddenly gave a start, raised its head, and looked at you. You pressed the button again. The sibolusovtus squeaked softly and toppled down unconscious next to the stump. 
You threw down the gun and happily grabbed the little beast...
jump.332.desc:
You pointed the thingamajig toward the peacefully sleeping sibolusovtus and pressed the red button.
Well, judging by the smell, you got a nice roast out of the little animal. The flamethrower worked gloriously...
jump.333.desc:
You directed the weapon toward the peacefully sleeping sibolusovtus and pulled the trigger. 
The meadow immediately became very cold. You blew on your frozen fingers and walked up to the stump. A large snowdrift rose in its place.
You burrowed into it a little and discovered that the sibolusovtus had turned into a chunk of ice. 
"Maybe it'll thaw while I carry it back to the base," you thought as you tried to pick it up.
A faint cracking noise could be heard, and the poor beast's head separated from its torso.
You looked on this scene darkly and walked away...
jump.334.text: Throw a jar of sulfuric acid into it...
jump.334.desc:
You swung your arm and heaved a vial of sulfuric acid at the stump. The stump joyfully smoked and melted away. 
It's not clear what you wanted to accomplish, but the sibolusovtus melted away along with the stump. Only the tip of its tail remained. Obviously, a memento...
jump.335.desc:
You vision didn't let you down, and you joyfully plucked up the plant.
"The gaal will be so happy, my precious," you remarked as you tucked the grass into your pocket.
jump.336.desc:
Cliffs towered proudly above you, obstructing the sun which occasionally crept out from the storm clouds. The result was a penetrating, chilling darkness.
You had already begun to complain to the world around you about the infinite injustice that would cause a gallant ranger to trudge along cold and hungry, with one foot in the grave... Then suddenly the sun peeked out and toasted you with its hot rays for several minutes, baking you up to a nice and crispy crust. When the sun again hid behind the clouds, you gave thanks; shook the embers off of your naked, charred skull; and carried on your way.
jump.337.text: Engage the monster in hand-to-hand combat...
jump.337.desc:
You threw yourself onto the monster despite the sudden weakness in your knees.
Nothing good came of this shenanigan. The monster literally smeared you across the wall, even though you were furiously pummeling his scaly head with the grip of your gun...
jump.338.text: Dart toward the sibolusovtus with your bare hands...
jump.338.desc:
You threw yourself at the sleeping little animal and grabbed it by the leg.
Out of fright and anger from being woken up, the beast let out an irate roar and chattered maliciously.
But since you were firmly holding it by the legs, it had nowhere to go, and you proudly dragged it back to the base...
jump.339.text: Dart toward the sibolusovtus with your bare hands...
jump.339.desc:
You issued a war cry and threw yourself onto the poor little beast sleeping on the small stump.
When it spit some kind of sticky gunk into your eyes, you realized that you had underestimated your enemy.
And by the time you had cleaned out your eyes enough to see anything, the sibolusovtus had vanished without a trace...
jump.344.text: Pick a subject: "The Proper Way to Dress an <clr>Auropedal Sibolusovtus<clrEnd>"...
jump.346.text: Pick a subject: "Naked, <clr>Leg-Eared<clrEnd> Fae Idly Splashes at <clr>sibolusovtus<clrEnd> in the Shower"...
jump.347.text: Put the sibolusovtus in the analyzer...
jump.347.desc: You grabbed the sibolusoft, which was lethargically trying to escape, threw it into the analyzer, and immediately slammed the door shut to keep it from getting out.
jump.348.desc:
You spit on the reference materials and decided to do it the old-school way, i.e. by trial-and-error.
The sibolusovtus watched you in horror, realizing that the jokes were over and that it was about to be carved up by a psycho ranger ignoramus, who had never cut up anything more complicated than a stick of sausage.
jump.349.desc: "The sibolusovtus is male. Confidence: 70%," read the analyzer's output.
jump.350.desc:
"The sibolusovtus is female. Confidence: 70%," read the analyzer's output.
So if the analyzer wasn't mistaken, the sibolusovtus wasn't the right gender and you would have to quickly go find another sibolusovtus of the right gender...
jump.352.text: Head off to search once again...
jump.352.desc:
Feeling very grumpy, you looked at the female sibolusovtus, which was chattering in her own incomprehensible, animal language. You were seized with such rage that you wanted to stuff her back into the analyzer and set the timer for an hour and a half, but you maintained control and only pushed her outside and wished her well.
There was nothing left for you to do now besides head out to look again...
jump.354.desc:
"The sibolusovtus is male. Confidence: 70%," read the analyzer's output.
So if the analyzer wasn't mistaken, the sibolusovtus was the right gender and you should quickly begin dismembering it...
jump.355.desc: "The sibolusovtus is female. Confidence: 70%," read the analyzer's output.
jump.357.desc: "Maybe the analyzer is wrong," you thought to yourself. "Maybe the sibolusovtus is actually a male. And I really, really don't want to go back into that wild jungle..."
jump.358.desc: You looked into the eyes of the poor little animal, which was pitifully wiping away tears with its snout, and you began to feel sorry for it...
jump.359.text: Administer a dose of sleeping aid to the sibolusovtus...
jump.359.desc: You injected a dose to the leg-eared and it immediately dozed off, glancing up at you with one eye from time to time. Obviously, one dose wasn't enough.
jump.360.text: Administer three doses of sleeping aid to the sibolusovtus...
jump.360.desc: You measured out and administered three doses of sleeping aid to the sibolusovtus. He instantly dropped off to sleep happily, and you prepared yourself for the dissection...
jump.361.text: Administer ten doses of sleeping aid to the sibolusovtus...
jump.361.desc:
The sibolusovtus twitched convulsively and died...
Frustrated, you looked at the lifeless body and headed toward the forest...
jump.362.text: Stun the sibolusovtus with a blow to the head...
jump.362.desc:
You took aim and struck the sibolusovtus on the noggin. It squealed resentfully and spit on you. You again tried to knock it out. In vain. Then you became complete unglued and... 
<clr>[What followed were scenes of hard core violence, so, in order to avoid a MATURE (+17) rating on this quest, this passage has been cut and replaced by a description of the life of deep-water eels]<clrEnd>
...eels are found at an average depth and, less often, in watering holes. While it is rare, they can be encountered where reeds grow. Each fall, the eels migrate south in droves to the upper reaches of the Aye-Notskats river, where they breed and spawn... 
<clr>[end of cut]<clrEnd>
...the sibolusovtus squeezed out a squawk and blacked out.
jump.363.desc:
You crossed your fingers and firmly tied the sibolusovtus to the operating table. Tears and cold sweat flowed down the poor little animal's snout.
"Well, why did your fellow clansman have to go and poison me?" you asked the sibolusovtus, feeling uneasy. "So go ahead and cry - or don't cry - but I'm not in the mood to die..."
jump.368.text: Go into the forest to look for a sibolusovtus
jump.368.desc: Thus, you found yourself in a dense, impassable forest. Hungry eyes stared at you from all sides, and various animals, insects, and other spawn of the forest breathed out nasty sounds. The swamp burped, the trees rustled, and sun shone down between the clouds. In one word - beauty.
jump.369.desc:
You shrank away from the stump and then stepped away for quite a distance. The idyllic atmosphere had disappeared instantly and you lost all desire for sleep.
You spit at the stump's eye from a distance, but missed. Then, utterly unglued, you decided to annihilate it to keep it from deceiving any more rangers...
jump.370.desc: You examined the unit, figured out approximately where its barrel was, pointed it at the stump, and prepared to attack...
jump.371.desc: You pressed the white button, but nothing happened. All the while, the stump continued to savagely bat its eyes at you and bare its crooked teeth...
jump.372.desc: You pressed the button as far as it would go and began kicking yourself that you didn't have any food with you... You could have had a nice little barbeque by the campfire.
jump.373.desc:
You pressed the button and a snowstorm pelted the stump, freezing everything around it.
You might think that a stump is a stump is a stump.
But whereas this stump used to be an ordinary stump, now it's a stump inundated with snow...
jump.375.text: Look in the pavilion marked "First Aid"
jump.383.text: Insert the gear you found into the opening in the lock...
jump.384.desc: "I've already got one like that," you thought and walked on...
jump.407.text: Spit on the stump and leave...
jump.418.text: Walk away from the warehouse doors...
jump.418.desc: You stepped sorrowfully away from the door, cursing these strange archaeologists who pack things where needed; but where it's not needed, they put tricky locks and other machines that are entirely unnecessary.
jump.419.desc: The gear fell out of the lock into your hands, and the door slowly opened...
jump.430.desc: You looked around at the bare walls one more time and went outside...
jump.443.desc:
When the poor sibolusovtus noticed you holding the saw, it was so frightened it gave up the ghost.
In a rage, you hurled the now-useless saw aside and again headed into the forest...
jump.444.desc:
As far as you understood, the sibolusovtus had to be sawn open at the third vertebrae... But the saw quickly spoiled all your plans, and in a minute lying in front of you there was a pile of shredded hide and fur, which had been the sibolusovtus not long ago...
You viciously hurled the saw onto the floor and again headed off to look for a sibolusovtus...
jump.445.desc:
You cut the sibolusovtus off at the fifth vertebrae and suddenly realized that it had nearly regained consciousness. 
You quickly dashed for the sleeping aid, but you were too late... The sibolusovtus died of fright when it saw its innards spilling out...
jump.446.desc: You carefully cut the sibolusovtus and, trembling, reached inside its body to get its poison sack.
jump.448.text: Head off to find a sibolusovtus...
jump.449.desc: For a few seconds the sibolusovtus watched in horror as  you cut it open, then it emitted a wild howl and died of fright and pain...
jump.450.desc:
You carefully cut the eerily chirping sibolusovtus and reached into the depths of its body to find its poison sack. 
The great interrogator in you must have died, because the sibolusovtus couldn't endure such torture - and it died of horror.
When you found the poison, you discovered it was unsuitable for use...
jump.451.text: Verify that the sibolusovtus you disemboweled is actually a male...
jump.451.desc: You began to painstakingly investigate the poison using a microscope. Five minutes later you discovered with delight that you weren't mistaken.
jump.452.text: Verify that the sibolusovtus you disemboweled is actually a male...
jump.452.desc:
You began to painstakingly investigate the poison using a microscope. Five minutes later you discovered with horror that the sibolusovtus was female.
This was probably the biggest disappointment of your life...
jump.454.desc:
"Oh!" you cried, throwing yourself onto gaal, thoroughly irrigating him with your tears of gratitude. "My dear fellow, I'm so happy to see you!"
"Yes, I can see that," said the gaal with a scrunched up face as he peeled you off. "And I see that the antidote worked." 
"Uh, you know... you're like.. like a brother to me! I found grass for you, didn't I?"
"Now that's something I want to hear," said the gaal, becoming noticeably happier. "Give it here."
"Just a sec," you said. Then you grabbed hold of the wall for stability and started rummaging through your pockets. "No, that's not it... and that's not it... what's that doing in there? Ah! Here it is!"
You offered the symgrass to the gaal, who immediately tried to run off somewhere.
"Stop!" you shouted and caught him by the arm. "Why in the world did they send me here anyway? I haven't fulfilled my mission yet..."
"Psh..." said the gaal, waving his arm away. "There was something, but now it's past. 
"Well, what was it?" you asked, uncomforted.
"Some Evil Genius turned the planet into his personal residence. 
"Oh, really?! I'll take care of him right now..." you said and gestured as if you were opening a bottle of beer.
"Too late. He must have learned of your arrival and sped off to a different end of the galaxy, but the base was loaded with landmines. It's been destroyed. And now if you will please excuse me. I need to go be treated."
"But..." you said, feeling a bit depressed. "Then let's say goodbye."
"Goodbye," said the gaal dryly. "By the way, don't deviate from your course to your destination. The antidote isn't a complete cure, so the poison will reach a lethal concentration again. You can get full treatment in a professional equipped clinic. I don't know how long the poison will be inactive - anywhere from a month to several decades - but you still shouldn't put off the antidote."
This news actually helped you sober up and, after shaking the gaal's hand again, you set off in search of your ship...

You took the assault blaster from you shoulder and shot the serenely sleeping sibolusovtus.

You decided to show the monster who had won first place at the races, and you took off with all your might. 
Soon the wheezing at your back died down and you gleefully realized that you had shaken it.
Soon the corridor came to an end and you again found yourself in the forest.
jump.480.desc:
You ran along the corridor to save yourself from the monster, who pranced after you, smacking and drooling and howling in anticipation of lunch. Despite your best efforts, you weren't able to outrun it. 
What's more, maybe it was just your imagination, but the monster seemed distended, as if it had been inflated with air; and you further noticed that this didn't make it run any slower, rather it howled and drooled at the more...

jump.518.desc:
You walked through the forest and suddenly fell face-first into some pit.
Curses passed your lips as you plummeted down dozens of meters and plopped into a swamp of muddy, stinking slush. 
In disgust, you spit out the gunk that had crowded into your mouth and suddenly saw a fighter on the far side of the swamp.
It was miraculously suspended over the swamp, even though its engine was turned off. And it reminded you of something a lot...
You suddenly heard voices and listened closely, risking sinking into the swamp.
"Believe in the force, Luke," croaked an old, probably-not-human voice.
"I can't do it," replied a more delicate, definitely-human voice. "I'll never be able to do this."
"You will," replied the other voice. "Let's try it again."
You watched as the fighter started smoothly from its place and flew stern-first toward you. You didn't like this. You tried swimming to the shore, but you didn't make it. The fighter hung over you and abruptly crashed into the swamp, as if it had instantly gone from light as a feather to heavy as a fighter.
A wave of swamp slush from the fallen fighter rolled over you, covering your head, and you lost consciousness.
But when you came to on the shore, neither the fighter nor the mysterious speakers were there.
jump.520.desc:
You spit on the reference materials and decided to do it the old-school way, i.e. by trial-and-error.
The sibolusovtus watched you in horror, realizing that the jokes were over and that it was about to be carved up by a psycho ranger ignoramus, who had never cut up anything more complicated than a stick of sausage.

The sight even made you feel ill. Meanwhile, a hole formed in the monster's chest and small slimy lumps crawled out in every direction.

You diligently spit all over the place and splashed into the water. 
Then there was nothing left for you to do but get yourself out of the cave and return to the surface.
jump.543.desc:
"Well, whatever will be, will be," you said recklessly and yanked the rusted level.
Beyond the hatch in the wall there was a dull rumbling, like the stomach of a cannibalistic troll. You weren't very pleased by this, but what was worse was the fact that the previously-dry floor was now slowly but surely being covered by murky water that was bleeding from the hatch, which was now slightly ajar.
You began running toward the water, but you weren't faster than an enormous rock which had plunked down right in the water and obstructed your way to safety.
jump.547.desc:
As you were going up, you couldn't help yourself and you peeked into the safe to see if it had anything useful or not.
You were utterly horrified out fell a fireproof, insoluble, and impact-resistant check for "Lyatseskish and Sons" Bank in the amount of 5,000 cr.
Being filled with a spiritual thrill, you froze and began to dive back down. When you had almost reached the bottom you remembered that you had forgotten to paddle up to the surface and, doubling your efforts, you rushed upward.
